description_full: Caledonia Mining Corporation Plc engages in the exploration, development, and production of gold in Zimbabwe. The company is also involved in the exploration and development of mineral properties for precious metals. It owns a 64% stake in the gold-producing Blanket Mine, 100% stake in the Bilboes Sulphide Project, and the Motapa and Maligreen gold mining claims in Zimbabwe. The company was incorporated in 1992 and is headquartered in Saint Helier, Jersey.
ceo_bio: Mr. John Mark Learmonth | CEO & Non-Independent Director | Age 61 | Compensation: $823,724 (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 2K people. Revenue per employee of $78K ranks in the bottom quartile among Basic Materials peers, with revenue growing 15%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $6K of free cash flow annually. CEO compensation is 11× revenue per employee (reasonable relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: Caledonia Mining Corporation Pl is a small-cap basic materials business with a $405M market cap on $183M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 15% against a 9% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 42%.

The business throws off $14M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.82× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 14× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 15% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 24% operating margin runs 15pp above the Basic Materials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.83x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-14.0% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 221 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 17% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 38% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 58% and a beta of 0.94, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.73 vs 5y 0.89), so read it loosely.
About $4.2M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 45% in the 2020 crash, 50% in the 2022 bear market and 86% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $19.06 (margin of safety -10%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 26%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $12.02 to $30.15 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Basic Materials peers: P/E 6.0 vs 16.3 and EV/EBITDA 2.5 vs 8.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 75% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 3.6% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 12.1% (vs the 8% bar).
The 3 covering analysts target $43.88 on average, 109% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 15% earns above the cost of capital of 9.3%, but the 6pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.77).
It runs a 42% gross margin and converts 8% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.82x.
ROE of 11% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.6x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $2.5M.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 14.7% over 3 years and 19.3% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 53% of profits supports about 8.1% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 25.0% on average.
Analysts expect 14.0% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 15.3%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 67%.
Insider trading is two-way: 3 purchases and 1 sale over the past year, net $741K bought.
It returns 3.4% a year to shareholders (2.7% in dividends).
The share count has grown 9.8% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
Short interest is elevated at 12.4% of the float, 8.8 days to cover.
people: With about 2,357 employees, each generates about $78K of revenue, 0.1x the Basic Materials median, and revenue has grown 14.8% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $6K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $824K (11x revenue per employee).
